hint.p: If differentiating the entire equation all at once is too much to keep track of, try differentiating the left and right sides separately.

solution.p: Differentiating the right side is straightfoward, and gives \frac{d}{dx} (5x + 10y) = 5+10 \frac{dy}{dx}
Equating the two sides gives e^{x^5 y} \left({5x^{4}} + x^5 \frac{dy}{dx}\right) = 5+10 \frac{dy}{dx}
